results.note: Ad episcopos regni — no English translation found despite searches of CCEL, Medieval Sourcebooks, and academic databases.
Ad proceres regni — included in Priscilla Throop's 'Hincmar of Rheims on kingship, divorce, virtues and vices' (MedievalMS, 2014).
Ad regem — no complete English translation identified. Fragmentary letter summaries appear in Epistolae database but these are not full translations.
Capitula in synodo — draft translation exists on Collaborative Hincmar Project blog but is unverified work-in-progress; no formal published translation found.

Capitula synodica — related to Hincmar's episcopal statutes; first episcopal capitulary has draft translation by Charles West (2016) on Collaborative Hincmar Project blog, but this is unverified; no formal published translation.
Carmina aliquot — minor poetic work (289 words); no English translation found in any source searched.
Consilium Hincmari — brief work (984 words); no English translation identified in academic or open-access sources.
Coronationes regiae — no English translation found despite searches of kingship-related medieval sources.
De causa Teutfridi presbyteri — draft English translation available on Collaborative Hincmar Project blog (work-in-progress, unverified); no formal published translation.
De cavendis vitiis et virtutibus exercendis — translated by Priscilla Throop in 'Hincmar of Rheims on kingship, divorce, virtues and vices' (MedievalMS, 2014, pp. 35-143).
De coercendis militum rapinis (Epistola 126) — translated by Sam Kaplan, Daniel Martin, and Lily Stewart (2013); academic publication.
De diversa animae ratione — no English translation found in published or academic sources.
De divortio Lotharii et Tetbergae — two major copyrighted translations exist: (1) Rachel Stone & Charles West (Manchester University Press, 2016); (2) Priscilla Throop (MedievalMS, 2014).
De fide Carolo regi servanda — no English translation found despite searches for royal loyalty and Carolingian political theory texts.
De institutione regia — no complete English translation identified. (Note: Jonas of Orléans wrote a different De institutione regia; may cause confusion in sources.)

De praedestinatione — this large work (168,601 words) is Hincmar's major theological treatise against Gottschalk. Genke & Gumerlock (2010) include five letters by Hincmar on predestination but not the full De praedestinatione; primary text remains untranslated.
De presbyteris criminosos — no English translation found in searches of canon law or ecclesiastical discipline texts.
De regis persona et regio ministerio — translated by Priscilla Throop in 'Hincmar of Rheims on kingship, divorce, virtues and vices' (MedievalMS, 2014, pp. 1-34).

De una et non trina deitate (60,545 words) — Hincmar's major trinitarian treatise against Gottschalk. George Tavard published scholarly analysis (Marquette, 1996) but this is secondary; primary text translation not found.
De verbis Psalmi — no English translation identified in biblical commentary sources or medieval studies collections.
De villa Noviliaco — minor property-related work (871 words); no English translation found.
De visione Bernoldi presbyteri — no English translation found in ecclesiastical vision literature sources.
Encomium S. Remigii — hagiographic eulogy (3,660 words); no English translation identified. Companion work Vita S. Remigii also lacks translation.

Epistola (single letter, 2,150 words) — fragmentary letter summaries appear in Epistolae database (epistolae.ctl.columbia.edu) but these are not full translations; unclear which specific epistola this refers to.
Explanatio in ferculum Salomonis — biblical commentary on Song of Solomon; no English translation found.
Expositiones — general biblical expositions (13,078 words); no English translation identified.
Instructio ad Ludovicum Balbum — pre-coronation instruction to Louis the Stammerer (2,170 words); no English translation found despite searches of royal advice literature.
Juramentum — brief oath-related work (1,513 words); no English translation found.
Praefatio — preface text (4,944 words); no English translation identified in sources.
Professio fidei — brief profession of faith (174 words); no English translation found.
Quae exsequi debeat episcopus — episcopal duties text (2,366 words); no English translation identified.
Vita S. Remigii — hagiography of Saint Remigius (23,016 words); no English translation found. Latin text available on Wikisource.

Epistolae (letter collection, 106,642 words) — five of Hincmar's letters included in copyrighted Genke & Gumerlock 'Gottschalk and a medieval predestination controversy' (Marquette, 2010); fragmentary summaries in Epistolae database; most of the collection remains untranslated.
Opuscula in causa Hincmari Laudunensis (147,909 words) — large polemical work concerning Hincmar of Laon; no English translation found despite searches of ecclesiastical conflict sources.
